newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerians vote in big numbers, no violence reported.
newsitem.headline: Algerians vote in big numbers, no violence reported.

text.p: Algerians voted in large numbers on Thursday in a controversial constitutional referendum that appeared to be passing without the attacks threatened by Islamic militants, official media said.
Seven hours after polls opened, more than half of Algeria's 16.4 million eligible voters had cast their ballots, Algerian state-run radio said, quoting the interior ministry.
Official media said voting was taking place peacefully and there were no reports of violence.

Residents in the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, said the army shelled mountains neary the city on Wednesday night, apparently trying to pre-empt any buildup of Moslem guerrillas. Blida is a route for Moslem guerrillas seeking to carry out attacks around Algiers.
The national vote turnout was 55.33 percent at 3 p.m (1400 GMT), compared to 45.82 percent in last year's presidential election at the same time, official figures showed.
However, Algerian television monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation said voter turnout was low in two Berber provinces where Berber-dominated parties had called for a boycott.
Moslem rebels, waging a five-year guerrilla war against the North African country's secular government, had vowed to disrupt the poll and warned Algerians not to vote.

Opposition parties either called for a boycott or urged a "no" vote on the changes, which would strengthen the position of President Liamine Zeroual and bar Islamic fundamentalists from seeking election.
